literal: With beasts, humans, they are like; shining books with the learned, the other people.
translation: The unlearned are to those who have mastered illustrious books as beasts are to human beings.
modern: விளங்குகின்ற சிறந்த நூல்களைக் கற்றவர்களோடு கல்லாதவர்களை ஒப்பிடுவது, மக்களோடு விலங்குகளை ஒப்பிடுவதற்குச் சமமாகும்.
explanation: This couplet establishes a stark analogy: the unlearned are to the learned what beasts are to humans. The phrase 'இலங்கு நூல்' (shining books) emphasizes that true learning enlightens the mind. The poet uses the sociative case suffixes 'ஒடு' and 'ஓடு' (with / compared to) to set up the direct comparison between the two pairs. Just as humans possess higher faculties that distinguish them from animals, those who have studied possess a refined understanding that fundamentally elevates them above the ignorant.
